maria-sec: Heads-up — dependency tokenlib v2.1.0 has a CVE reported (public GitHub PoC) affecting KMS token handling. Fix requires a restart of the token-proxy sidecar + a small RBAC audit-schema tweak. Need prioritization: SLA impact vs public exposure.
jonathan: CVSS? exploitability? any active exploit reports?
maria-sec: CVSS 7.5, requires local access that can be chained from a misconfigured token endpoint. There is a limited PoC posted but no verified in-the-wild cases. Affects hosted + dedicated + private if they run token-proxy unpatched.
kevin-sre: Restarting token-proxy sidecars will drop KV cache briefly — could add ~50-200ms tail latency, and we will lose some in-memory cache entries. For Dedicated pools we can do rolling restarts. For hosteds we can route to fallback model variants if latency spike > SLO.
olivia-eng: Confirmed: the RBAC schema change is a harmless column add to audit_events and a short migration that locks the table for ~5s per shard. Rolling migration recommended. Canary plan: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%. Prefer off-peak (Sun 02:00 UTC).
sec-ops-bot: New vuln ticket created: VULN-2026-0417. Impact: tokenlib KMS handling. Affected services: token-proxy, kms-client. Suggested severity: high.
product-ops: Which customer tiers need immediate notice? We should notify Dedicated customers with SLA contracts and Private on-prem customers that opt-in for security advisories. Public advisory timing?
maria-sec: Recommend: prioritize Dedicated and Private high-tier customers for accelerated rollout within 72 hours. Hosted: schedule canary Sunday then staged rollout over 5 days. Hold public advisory 48h after patch pushed to all Dedicated and Canary complete to avoid giving exploit details.
jonathan: SLA impact matrix: if we do rolling restarts during work hours there's risk of hitting 99th perc latency SLO for a subset. For Dedicated customers with latency SLAs, propose maintenance window with customer notice and optional opt-out for strict real-time services.
kevin-sre: Operational checklist draft:
- create canary pool: pool=tokenlib-canary
- deploy patched token-proxy image to canary
- run migration with --non-blocking flag where available, otherwise apply shard-by-shard
- watch metrics: token_proxy_error_rate, kms_client_reauths, tail_latency_p99, db_lock_waits
- rollback triggers: >5x baseline error rate or p99 > 2x SLO for >10m
Command snippets:
```
kubectl set image deployment/token-proxy token-proxy=registry.redwood/token-proxy:2.1.1 -n redwood-serving --selector=pool=tokenlib-canary
# migration per shard
python tools/db_migrate.py --table audit_events --shard {shard} --no-wait
```

olivia-eng: I'll own the rollout plan + automation. Kevin, can you own monitoring and rollback runbook? Maria will own customer comms. Product-ops to prepare targeted emails to Dedicated customers.
product-ops: Will draft notices. For Private on-prem customers we should include KB steps for manual patch and migration script.
maria-sec: Agreed. Action items: Olivia create canary job by EOD, Kevin prepare dashboards and alerts, Product-ops draft notices for Legal review. We also need a short post-mortem template if anything goes south.
jonathan: One more: confirm KMS integration doesn't require key rotation for patched clients. Maria?
maria-sec: No key rotation required, but we recommend a one-time re-auth to pick up token format changes. I'll add to comms.
kevin-sre: Scheduling: Canary Sun 02:00 UTC, Canary evaluation window 4 hours, staged rollout Mon-Wed nights 02:00-06:00 UTC, full complete by Thu 06:00 UTC.
maria-sec: Thanks all. Marking owners in vuln ticket. Will update thread with ticket link and customer list. :thumbsup:
